title: P112: prove the invoice floor for mixed two-port factor terms
body:
## Result

Every rational strict fit of the fixed P112 full-group mask costs at least **334** if each rank-one term has at most two scalar source ports **or** at most two scalar reader ports. The sparse side may differ between terms, and the two orientation classes may cancel at forbidden entries. There is no rank or term-count restriction.

Thus any cheaper decoder needs a term that is dense on **both** sides. The proof treats the complete matrix equation as one gain graph on matrix positions, preserves repeated-factor gains consistently, and normalizes the recovered diagonal. It transfers termwise support envelopes to characteristic two, where the authenticated whole-group expansion is I334. Permitted free coefficients may change; exact endpoint preservation is not claimed by this general theorem.

The result also strengthens the necessary splitting budget: choose source or reader splitting separately for each term. Every proposed cost-at-most-296 decoder needs at least **38 units** of the resulting minimum per-term splitting overhead. A common within-group similarity may expose the mixed sparsity without changing any tariff.

The package retains a separate exact-canonical-endpoint companion for mixed two-mark coefficient queries and two-port actual readers, plus the uniform-side and bridge results with their precise hypotheses.

## Verification

- Independent written proofs audit repeated gains, essential cross-orientation cancellations, nonzero tree diagonals and shared normalization. An optional refinement preserves the endpoint's entire zero/nonzero pattern while allowing free values to change.
- Two independent geometry implementations authenticate all 111,556 symbolic expansion positions, the 28 free group pairs and the canonical invoice, including the residual 6+1 refinement.
- Exact controls cover a replicated balanced cycle, a surviving unbalanced cycle, a mixed I3 with forbidden-entry cancellations, and characteristic-two row/column normalization with an exact duplicated-mark endpoint.
- All three registered standard-library commands, metadata and committed-byte/source-history checks pass at `61e34922dfcc9a31ea3f9c753041ad10c8810d31`.
- The official Git-free export passes all three commands with empty PATH and read-only files; all 19 exported file hashes remain unchanged (0.50 seconds, Python 3.12.14 on Windows).

Reproduce: `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-sparse-gain-transfer`.

## Scope and provenance

This is a structural exclusion and necessary budget test. It does not establish a universal 334 floor for dense factors, provide a cheaper decoder or native schedule, or change the selected multiplication bound. Native storage, restoration, precision and all-size supplier obligations remain open.

Canonical main was refreshed before publication and remains `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244` (priority revision 7). The assigned decoder goal is recorded as a scope change. The complete 354-open-PR snapshot was supplemented by a current update-ordered delta scan; fresh Discussion coverage remains unavailable after persistent HTTP 406, so no exhaustive novelty claim is made.

Standard gain-graph rank facts and predecessor P112 cover/pricing work retain their source attribution. The mixed transfer and invoice deductions are proved here. Prepared by flyingviper with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate AI-agent checks; no independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed. Apache-2.0.
